title: Adversary skill levels (low-skilled vs high-skilled / zero-days); motivation
goal_html: Students analyze adversary profiles, assign skill tiers, and justify their reasoning using the feature-based classification rules from the lesson. Ties to LO 1.3.A (assess adversary capability and motivation to analyze risk).
reference_html:
Profile cards (print or display)

Profile Uses zero-day Custom tooling Targets specific victim Off-the-shelf only Adapts to defenses
Alex No No No Yes No
Blake Yes Yes Yes No Yes
Casey No No Yes No Yes
Dana No Yes No No No
Emery No No Yes Yes No
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation and sorts the on-screen adversary profiles into LOW and HIGH tiers, recording their reasoning for each.
  2. After completing the sim, pairs apply the same rules to the five profile cards above and record a tier and one-sentence justification for each.
  3. Pairs compare answers with the pair next to them. For any disagreement, they cite the specific rule from interface.md that resolves the dispute.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "threat analyst" (applies the rules mechanically), the other is the "risk manager" (challenges edge cases and asks "what if one feature changed?"). Swap roles for the second half of the profile cards.
exit_html: Each student submits: the tier they assigned to Casey (profile 3) and the rule number from interface.md that determined it, plus one sentence explaining why motivation (the goal of the attack) matters when assigning risk level.
